title.narrative: Providing access to essential basic life-saving quality health care, Nutrition and GBV services to affected IDPs, people in extremely-hard-to reach areas of Konduga and Mafa LGAs of Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtIn addressing the multi-faceted humanitarian crisis coupled with food insecurity and aftermath of flooding with displacement of people and the projected number of 2.6 million children under five that will face malnutrition (SAM and MAM), diseases outbreak, protection issues leading to mortality and morbidity, RHHF and FRAD will be implementing a multi-sectoral integrated life-saving essential quality health and nutrition care services mainstreaming GBV services for six (6) months to meet the need of 21,119 affected individuals with proposed activities not limited to the following.ltbrgtThe health component of the intervention will address gaps in essential primary healthcare by deploying mobile medical outreach teams and strengthening existing health facilities. Services will include immunization, treatment of common illnesses, antenatal and postnatal care, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and emergency disease surveillance and outbreak response. The intervention will contribute directly to Health Sector Strategic Objectives SSO1 and SSO2, aiming to reduce morbidity and mortality, particularly during the peak lean season when disease outbreaks and service inaccessibility are at their worst. Trained community health volunteers (CHVs), nurses, and CHEWs will ensure timely access and continuity of care in remote communities.ltbrgtThis project will provide integrated preventive and curative nutrition services to 21,119 children under five and pregnant and breastfeeding women (PBWG). Activities include mass and family MUAC screening, treatment of SAM and MAM through OTPs and targeted supplementary feeding, skilled MIYCN counselling, and distribution of micronutrient supplements and cash/voucher assistance. Nutrition interventions will be closely linked with hygiene promotion and GBV risk mitigation and aligned with Sector Objective 1 to reduce malnutrition-related morbidity and mortality.ltbrgtThe GBV component will be mainstreamed to the health components in Konduga and to the Nutrition components in Konduga and Mafa LGA to reach women and girls with lifesaving prevention and response services. Community awareness sessions will address GBV and Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA), while advocacy with sectors such as food security and livelihoods will help tackle the root causes of survival-based exploitation. The project will empower local structures, enhancing community-driven solutions, and mainstreaming protection across all activities. Special attention will be given to the inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups through participatory approaches and referral linkages. ltbrgtlt/pgt
